column1: # design/pintag-baseline.tsv — the pins whose untagged-ness this control records, and why.
# `scripts/design-pintag.sh` answers, for every pinned module of this tree's index, whether
# the pin is at a tagged release or whether its untagged-ness is explained: one CHANGELOG
# commit above a tag (or a chain of them, all CHANGELOG commits), the commit that installs
# tag-on-merge, or a repository that does not run tag-on-merge at all. Everything else is the
# signal — a merge above a tag that wrote no CHANGELOG commit — and it FAILS unless a row here
# records it.
# A row is module, commit, state, reason. The commit is part of the key: when a pin advances
# the row no longer matches the tree, and the control fails until the new pin is examined and
# the row is re-argued or lowered. A row whose pin becomes healthy is stale in the other
# direction and fails the same way. Delete the last row and the control is a plain check with
# nothing to excuse.
# These two rows are the live instances the control found on this tree: the failure mode that
# had no detector before it. Each was confirmed against the remote with
# `git ls-remote --tags <repo> | grep -F <sha>` returning nothing AND
# `git ls-remote <repo> refs/heads/main` returning the same sha — so the branch tip itself is
# untagged, not a pin that trails a tagged tip. They retire when tag-on-merge writes the
# missing CHANGELOG commit for those merges; the row is lowered in that change.
# tracked-by: opencharly/opencharly#793 — the gap the live instances were filed under (the mechanism is opencharly/.github#286)
# The three rows below record a DIFFERENT mechanism, added by the change that advanced these
# pins (the S3 word-list sweep of plugin-punktfunk#20, plugin-agent-pi#11 and plugin-gh#13).
# Each of those merges is a squash above a tag with no CHANGELOG commit above it, so the pin is
# untagged — but the reason is not #286's missed release: `tag-on-merge` FAILED AT THE RUN LEVEL
# on all three repos, with NO JOB EVER STARTED (`jobs: []` on the failed run, whose name is
# `.github/workflows/tag-on-merge.yml`). That is the org-wide "workflow file issue" of
# 2026-11-10, opencharly/.github#192 — and it persisted on these repos after the caller was
# reconciled with the canonical template at 07:1x-07:5xZ, so the reconcile did not fix it.
# Each row retires when tag-on-merge writes the missing CHANGELOG commit for its merge; the row
# is lowered in that change, exactly like every other row here.
# tracked-by: opencharly/.github#192 — the tag-on-merge breakage that wrote no CHANGELOG commit
